title: Mechanistic Interpretability of Protein Language Models Reveals Encoded Structural and Functional Properties of Intrinsically Disordered Proteins
abstract: Protein language models (PLMs) such as ESM-2 encode protein sequences as embeddings for downstream tasks. PLMs are trained on a masked learning objective that leverages evolutionary constraints. While interpretability studies of ESM-2 have focused on folded proteins, their behavior on intrinsically disordered proteins (IDPs), which constitute a substantial fraction of the human proteome and are implicated in numerous diseases, remains understudied. Because IDPs experience different types of evolutionary constraints on their amino acid sequences, we hypothesized that PLMs would behave differently on disordered versus folded regions. Here we show that ESM-2 exhibits reduced attention on disordered regions, yet still encodes meaningful biological signals. The model assigns heightened attention to disease-relevant residues even at high levels of disorder. Moreover, we show that both the radius of gyration and individual dynamic contact maps, key characteristics of IDPs, can be obtained from the model logits and embeddings. These findings suggest PLMs capture valuable information relevant to IDP biology despite their bias toward structured residues.

llm.novelty_zh: 首次系统地用机理可解释性方法检验蛋白语言模型 ESM-2 在无序蛋白（IDP）区域的注意力与编码内容，并证明其 logits 和嵌入可还原回转半径与动态接触图。
llm.summary_zh: 该研究考察蛋白语言模型 ESM-2 在无序蛋白（IDPs）上的行为，发现模型对无序区域的注意力降低，但仍编码了有意义的生物信号。模型对疾病相关残基保持较高关注，并且可以从 logits 与嵌入中恢复 IDP 的关键结构特征（回转半径与动态接触图）。工作属于蛋白语言模型可解释性研究，与虚拟细胞主题只有间接关系。

title: PerturbBridge: Conditional Latent Schr dinger Bridge for Single-Cell Perturbation Prediction
abstract: \textbf{Motivation:}Single-cell perturbation prediction seeks to recover transcriptional responses to unseen interventions from unpaired control and perturbed populations. The Schr\"odinger Bridge provides a principled framework for modeling these transitions as stochastic transport, but learning bridge dynamics directly from high-dimensional, sparse gene-expression profiles remains challenging. \textbf{Results:} We present PerturbBridge, a conditional latent Schr\"odinger Bridge framework for single-cell perturbation response prediction. A response-anchored autoencoder constructs a compact cellular representation that preserves dominant transcriptional response directions identified from training perturbations while encoding complementary cellular variation. In this latent space, PerturbBridge models conditional stochastic transport through a tractable approximation to the Schr\"odinger Bridge. We introduce the Perturbation-Induced Bridge Transformer, which uses perturbation and time-dependent slots to guide interactions among latent coordinates during drift estimation. Evaluations on Norman, Sci-Plex3, and Replogle RPE1 demonstrate leading performance in differential-expression direction recovery and perturbation-effect correlation, alongside competitive gene-expression prediction accuracy. \textbf{Availability:} The source code is available at \url{https://github.com/echQoQ/PerturbBridge}, with an archived version at \url{https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.24272128}.
